sources.title: “Bentogypsum”, a phosphoric acid purification residue: Characterization and implications for environmental and human health risk in Gabes (SE Tunisia)
sources.institution: R. B. El Zrelli et al., Journal of Hazardous Materials (Elsevier), vol. 508
sources.summary: Peer-reviewed study of a waste called bentogypsum, produced when the Tunisian Chemical Group purifies phosphoric acid in Gabès and stored in open-air stockpiles. It characterises the waste physically, mineralogically and chemically, then runs a screening-level assessment of environmental and human health risk. Received 24 September 2025, accepted 11 March 2026, published online 13 March 2026. Supplementary tables are not part of the PDF used for this record.

findings.headline: Bentogypsum contains 337 mg/kg of cadmium
findings.summary: The study reports an average cadmium concentration of 337 ± 21 mg/kg in bentogypsum (n = 3). Cadmium is the highest of all trace elements measured in the waste. For comparison, the paper lists 48 mg/kg for phosphate…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum contains 59.0 mg/kg of arsenic
findings.summary: Average arsenic concentration of 59.0 ± 2.1 mg/kg (n = 3). The paper lists 3.1 mg/kg for phosphate rock, 1 mg/kg for phosphogypsum and 30.2 mg/kg for phosphogypsum foam, so bentogypsum is the highest of the four…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum contains 15 mg/kg of lead
findings.summary: Average lead concentration of 15 ± 3 mg/kg (n = 3). The paper lists 4.1 mg/kg for phosphate rock, 0.9 mg/kg for phosphogypsum and 5.8 mg/kg for phosphogypsum foam, so bentogypsum is the highest of the four materials for…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum contains about 125 mg/kg of chromium
findings.summary: Average chromium concentration of 125 ± 6 mg/kg in Table 4 (n = 3). Phosphate rock (154 mg/kg) and phosphogypsum foam (412 mg/kg) are higher in the paper's comparison; phosphogypsum (13 mg/kg) is lower.

findings.headline: Bentogypsum contains 46.3 mg/kg of thorium
findings.summary: Average thorium concentration of 46.3 ± 5.3 mg/kg (n = 3). The paper lists 11.2 mg/kg for phosphate rock, 0.74 mg/kg for phosphogypsum and 14 mg/kg for phosphogypsum foam, so bentogypsum is the highest of the four…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum contains 35 mg/kg of uranium
findings.summary: Average uranium concentration of 35 ± 3 mg/kg (n = 3). The paper lists 41 mg/kg for phosphate rock, 1.6 mg/kg for phosphogypsum and 56 mg/kg for phosphogypsum foam, so bentogypsum ranks third of the four materials for…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum ranks highest of four phosphate-industry materials for 10 trace elements
findings.summary: Comparing bentogypsum with phosphate rock, phosphogypsum and phosphogypsum foam from the same industrial site, the paper reports bentogypsum as highest for ten elements: As, Cd, Ge, In, Pb, Re, Se, Sn, Th and Tl. On…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum is strongly acidic: pH 1.15
findings.summary: The average pH of bentogypsum was 1.15 ± 0.11 (n = 3), lower than phosphogypsum (2.20) and phosphogypsum foam (2.36). The authors state that this strong acidity increases how easily pollutants leach out of the waste and…

findings.headline: Fluoride makes up 13.2% of bentogypsum by dry weight
findings.summary: Fluoride averaged 13.22% of dry weight (13.2 ± 0.6% in Table 3), the highest of the four materials compared (phosphate rock 3.42%, phosphogypsum 1.66%, phosphogypsum foam 2.32%). Sodium oxide (Na2O) was also highest in…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum is very fine-grained: median grain size 2.88 µm
findings.summary: Median grain size is 2.88 µm and average grain size 2.71 µm; the paper describes essentially all grains as smaller than 20 µm, in the clayey-silt range. The authors link this fine size to wind-driven erosion and…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum is a mix of calcium sulfates and fluoride-bearing minerals
findings.summary: X-ray diffraction identified gypsum (26.42%), malladrite (24.42%), anhydrite (16.70%), heklaite (15.05%), bassanite (8.95%) and haigerachite (8.10%). Malladrite and heklaite are fluoride-bearing silicates. Bentonite…

findings.headline: Bentogypsum is kept in open-air stockpiles less than 500 m from urban areas
findings.summary: The authors report that the purification residue has been stored in the open air since the early 2000s, described as temporary storage, on a 2.5-hectare site less than 500 m from urban areas. They add that a planned…

findings.headline: About 730,000 tonnes of wet residue stored since 2005
findings.summary: The authors estimate about 730 × 10³ tonnes of wet bentogypsum stored at the site since 2005, with current production of about 100 tonnes per day (about 36,500 tonnes per year).

findings.headline: Four pollution indices place bentogypsum in their highest classes
findings.summary: Using six metals (As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Pb, Zn) the paper reports: contamination degree 3899 (very high), pollution load index 14.94 (polluted), geoaccumulation index 46.25 (extremely contaminated) and potential ecological…

findings.headline: Cadmium accounts for 94.58% of the toxic units
findings.summary: Of the toxic-unit total for the six metals considered, cadmium contributes 94.58%, followed by arsenic (3.44%), chromium (1.37%), zinc (0.30%), lead (0.16%) and copper (0.15%).

findings.headline: Non-cancer hazard index for children: 10.99 (above 1)
findings.summary: For a modelled child, the combined non-cancer hazard index (HI) for six metals is 10.99 ± 0.61. Values above 1 indicate a potential non-cancer health concern in this method. The authors describe children as about 9…

findings.headline: Non-cancer hazard index for adults: 1.24 (above 1)
findings.summary: For a modelled adult, the combined non-cancer hazard index is 1.24 ± 0.07, slightly above the value of 1 used as the concern level.

findings.headline: Total cancer risk for children: 2.98 × 10⁻² (limit used: 10⁻⁴)
findings.summary: Table 6 gives a total carcinogenic risk (TCR) of 2.98 × 10⁻² ± 1.81 × 10⁻³ for a modelled child, based on arsenic, cadmium, chromium and lead. The authors compare it with an upper limit of 10⁻⁴ and conclude the waste…

findings.headline: Total cancer risk for adults: 3.20 × 10⁻³ (32 times the 10⁻⁴ limit)
findings.summary: Table 6 gives a total carcinogenic risk of 3.20 × 10⁻³ ± 1.95 × 10⁻⁴ for a modelled adult, which the authors state is 32 times the 10⁻⁴ upper limit they use.

findings.headline: Swallowing is the dominant exposure route in the risk calculation
findings.summary: In the modelled scenarios, ingestion accounts for 98% of cancer risk for both children and adults, with skin contact about 1.4% (children) and 1.7% (adults) and inhalation under 0.05%. For non-cancer risk, ingestion…

findings.headline: Cadmium drives most of the calculated health risk
findings.summary: Across all exposure routes, cadmium accounts for 68% of the non-cancer risk for children and 70% for adults, and for 92% of the cancer risk for both children and adults.

findings.headline: The landfill liner is torn and sinking in places, with no leachate treatment
findings.summary: The authors describe a 1.5 mm HDPE geomembrane over about 20 cm of compacted clay, installed in 2005, with a drainage ditch but no leachate treatment system. They report greenish drainage water standing around the…

findings.headline: Authors estimate the waste's weight far exceeds what the liner can bear
findings.summary: The authors state that the vertical stress from the waste is about 30 t/m², about 14 times the typical tensile strength and about 7 times the puncture threshold they cite for a 1.5 mm HDPE geomembrane, and propose this…

findings.headline: Stockpiles about 12 m high with little dust protection; summer winds from the east and northeast
findings.summary: The authors report stockpiles about 12 m high, protected only by a wall about 3.5 m high and a sparse vegetation screen, and say there is no other protection against dust. They state prevailing summer winds come mainly…

findings.headline: Authors say leachate may reach groundwater used for drinking and irrigation
findings.summary: The authors state that the liner does not effectively stop drainage water from infiltrating the sandy bedrock and reaching groundwater, which they say neighbouring inhabitants of Chatt Sidi Abd Essalam use for irrigated…

findings.headline: Authors report illnesses among neighbours, but no epidemiological study exists
findings.summary: From field observations (asking inhabitants and factory workers), the authors report cases of serious non-cancer illnesses and cancers, mainly lung, bone, prostate and kidney, among people living near the dumpsite. They…

findings.headline: The risk assessment is a screening, not a prediction of illness
findings.summary: The authors state that the indices are a tier-1 screening of the waste's intrinsic hazard under plausible exposure scenarios. They do not aim to predict actual disease or ecological damage. The paper also notes the lack…

findings.headline: Authors conclude bentogypsum is hazardous waste and call for urgent action
findings.summary: The authors conclude that bentogypsum should be classified as hazardous industrial waste, not an inert by-product. They recommend containment and isolation of existing stockpiles, leachate and dust control, treatment or…
